chunks: Abu Basir narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, Adam عليه السلام was the one who built the House, laid its foundation, and was the first to cover it with hair. He was also the first to perform hajj to it. Then after Adam عليه السلام, Tubbaʿ covered it with leather, then Ibrahim عليه السلام covered it with palm-leaf mats. The first to clothe it with garments was Sulayman ibn Dawud عليه السلام; he covered it with Qibati cloth.

key_terms.آدَمَ: Adam عليه السلام, identified here as the builder of the House
key_terms.أَسَاسَهُ: its foundation, referring to the base of the House
key_terms.الثِّيَابَ: cloth garments used as a covering
key_terms.الْبَيْتَ: the Sacred House, meaning the Kaʿbah
key_terms.الْخَصَفَ: woven palm-leaf mats or plaited covering
key_terms.حَجَّ: performed hajj, the pilgrimage to the Sacred House

ai.seo_question: Who first built and covered the Kaʿbah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts an early sacred history of the Kaʿbah, attributing its building and first covering to Adam عليه السلام. It then describes successive coverings by Tubbaʿ, Ibrahim عليه السلام, and Sulayman ibn Dawud عليه السلام, highlighting the House’s ancient sanctity and connection to hajj.
